title: sfh run status
description: The atomic status.json snapshot in an sfh run directory. Readers must ignore unknown properties for forward compatibility.

terminal.description: Whether this state is final. Added in v1.2.0 to `status --json`; absent from older writers.

run_id.description: The run directory's own name. Added in v1.2.0.

implicit_target.description: True when no run directory was named and sfh selected the NEWEST run. A caller that wants to be sure it is reporting on its own run should pass the run dir explicitly. Added in v1.2.0.

command.description: The sfh command that produced this envelope. Part of the common machine envelope added in v1.2.0.

ok.description: Whether the command succeeded. Part of the common machine envelope added in v1.2.0.

next_actions.description: Follow-ups, never prose. Added in v1.2.0. `why` and `wait` are always runnable: just `kind` and `argv`. Since v1.4.0, `resume` and `carry_budget` are diagnosed instead of assumed from state alone: they add `resumable`/`carryable`, `reason` and `requires`, and `argv` is present only when the action can actually succeed - an action that cannot is still reported, with `reason` explaining why, rather than silently omitted.

argv.description: A runnable command, never prose. Present unconditionally for why/wait; for resume/carry_budget, present only when resumable/carryable is true.

resumable.description: kind: resume only. Whether resuming this run can actually continue it - false for, e.g., a persistence failure or a stuck run that exhausted max_visits, where resuming would only repeat the same dead end. Added in v1.4.0.

carryable.description: kind: carry_budget only. Whether this run's spend is confirmed final (see the durable run_end / positive-stop rules) and therefore safe to carry into a corrected flow. Added in v1.4.0.

reason.description: kind: resume/carry_budget. Why the action is, or is not, runnable right now. Added in v1.4.0.

requires.description: kind: resume/carry_budget. Extra flags this run's resume needs before it can succeed, e.g. "--adopt-workspace" for workspace drift or "--force-resume" for a changed execution closure - already the flags argv carries when resumable is true. Empty when nothing extra is required. Added in v1.4.0.
